decisions.body: Decision A′, folded into the change artifacts on the task branch (commit f923f2e9): read design D4 as amended and D15–D18, proposal FR13–FR16 and the split NFR-S1, tasks 3.0, 3.0a, 3.3, 3.3a, 3.6, 5.1, 5.1a, 5.3, 6.3, 6.4, and the new deltas plugin/github-plugin, plugin/plugin-discovery. github-actions is a core built-in in the new module adapters/scm beside scm-status; the vendor bundle keeps the tracker only; the GitHub HTTP core moves to the library :githubapi and the egress allowlist to the leaf :httpegress (rule of two, manual-sync-pairs.md as revised on main). The pin survives as the describe flag checkIdIsPinnedPath. R1–R6, D13 and D14 stand. Resume fix-artifacts from the updated artifacts; the remaining MODIFIED blocks you listed are written.
decisions.author: tracker

decisions.body:
(1) Option A: a passing verdict keeps its below-threshold findings. Both premises behind the findings-less pass were checked: FR4 of add-stage-engine (findings are retry feedback) and FR8/D6 of add-manual-run (the exit code is the verdict, the file on exit 0 is ignored). D5 of this change removed the second one, and the first no longer holds alone: the state file, `status --json` and the usage report are consumers too. Industry practice is the same shape (GitHub code scanning records alerts below the failure threshold; Trivy separates --severity from --exit-code).

The decision is folded into the artifacts on the task branch, commit 924f92ac:
- design.md: D5 as amended, with the verified premises and the rejected alternative (narrowing the scenario); a new D9 row "The findings of a pass" with writers, readers and the enforcement
- proposal.md: FR7 extended
- tasks.md: 2.2a (Verdict.Pass(runUrl, findings); VerdictDerivation fills the below-threshold results; StateJsonMapper, AttemptMapper and UsageReportJsonMapper carry them through the existing findings field; CheckFindings.noteIgnoredOnPass deleted; a spec that a pass's findings feed no retry) and 2.2b (the same for the judge)
- specs/verification/verdict-executors: requirement "A pass keeps its below-threshold findings" with two scenarios

Note the second instance of the same defect, which the escalation did not list: JudgeVerdictExtractor returns an empty Pass on "passed": true. That is task 2.2b; the judge classes stay exempt from the derivation gate (D9, NG1).

(2) Option (a): main is fixed. #124 adds a reasoned exemption row for .gnomish/stages/usage-report/report.sh to UsageFoldOwnerBoundarySpec (the factory runs from the v0.1.0 release, which has no `usage --markdown`; the row is asserted reached, so it is deleted with the fold). main (#123, #124) is merged into the task branch as 15419d88. Do not re-touch the spec or the script.

Continue from task 2.2, then 2.2a and 2.2b.

report.question:
migrate-verify-to-executor-contract: tasks 2.2, 2.2b, 2.3 are done and ticked. Two items cannot be finished without an artifact edit this stage may not make.

(1) Missing delta for cli/manual-run (blocks the last item of 2.2a and all of 3.2).
Task 2.2a and the D9 row 'The findings of a pass' delete CheckFindings.noteIgnoredOnPass and the exit-0 findings-file drop (adapters/.../check/CheckFindings.java:61, ShellCommandCheckRunner.java:233). FR5 and the verdict-executors delta ('A shell exit code SHALL carry no verdict meaning') make the shell answer SARIF, with the exit code as status only.
The main spec openspec/specs/cli/manual-run/spec.md still binds the old behaviour, and no delta of this change touches cli/manual-run (verified: the only active delta there, add-pipeline-routing, modifies 'Run selects a pipeline explicitly or by default' only):
- requirement 'Command check runner' (:133): exit 0 -> Pass, 126/127 -> CannotVerify, other non-zero -> Fail;
- requirement 'Findings-JSON wire format' (:154): the file replaces the synthetic finding only after a non-zero exit; scenario 'A findings file on a green check is ignored' (:170);
- requirement 'files_exist builtin runner' (:117): verdict wording 'Fail with exactly two findings', which still holds through derivation.
Implementing 3.2 or the 2.2a deletion against these scenarios would narrow stable scenarios with no decision behind it, which spec-mismatch.md forbids. A scenario cannot be dropped through MODIFIED (delta-specs.md), so the fix is a cli/manual-run delta in this change that REMOVEs 'Command check runner' and 'Findings-JSON wire format', or MODIFIes them keeping every scenario title and rewording each THEN to the derived form. Their kept duties (sh -c through exec(), output tail, GNOMISH_FINDINGS_FILE allocation, env allowlist, 127 -> infrastructure) move to verdict-executors if REMOVEd.
So far the shell keeps the exit-code semantics (exit 0 -> empty SARIF; non-zero -> failed/quality; 126/127 -> failed/infrastructure), routed through VerdictDerivation.

(2) Task 2.4 asks to 'add JudgeCannotVerify to D9's exempt list'. That is an edit of design.md, which this stage may not make. The spec half is done: OutcomeClassifierOwnerSpec has the judge rows retagged with the pickup 'extract-agent-round-runner: ' and no row with this change's name.

Also for your review: (a) 2.2 added two VerdictAnswer variants, QualityFailure and InfrastructureFailure. They mirror the contract's failed/quality and failed/infrastructure statuses, so a provider's Fail([]) or a command's non-zero exit is not read as an empty, passing SARIF. (b) 2.3 routed RoundRecords' two verdicts (a failed/quality round, the empty chain) through VerdictDerivation. D9 did not list them.

Recommended: A. Without it, 3.2 would narrow stable scenarios, and the remaining tasks 2.4 through 7.2 would wait one more round.
options: A: fold a cli/manual-run delta into the change (MODIFY 'Command check runner' and 'Findings-JSON wire format' to the derived form, keeping every scenario title, or REMOVE them and move their kept duties to verdict-executors), add JudgeCannotVerify to D9's exemptions, then resume at 2.2a's last item and 2.4

B: keep the exit-code semantics of the shell for this change: drop the noteIgnoredOnPass deletion from 2.2a and D9, and narrow FR5 and 3.2 to the legacy findings file; a later change owns the shell's SARIF-only answer
